en.title: Edinburgh Film Festival Sets 2027 Dates for Milestone 80th Edition
en.summary: The iconic Edinburgh International Film Festival has officially announced its dates for the 2027 edition, promising a celebration of its rich history and a look towards the future of cinema. This milestone event will mark 80 years of showcasing groundbreaking films and nurturing new talent.
en.body:
The Edinburgh International Film Festival (EIFF), a cornerstone of the UK's cinematic calendar, has revealed that its 80th edition will take place from August 12th to August 18th, 2027. This significant milestone edition is poised to honor the festival's illustrious legacy, which has seen it premiere seminal works like **Blade Runner**, **Alien**, and **Withnail & I**, while simultaneously building on the revitalized energy of its recent iterations. Supported by Screen Scotland, the festival continues its mission to champion independent cinema and discover emerging filmmakers.

The 2027 dates follow closely on the heels of the 79th edition, scheduled for August 13th to 19th, 2026. That 2026 program is set to be a vibrant showcase of global filmmaking, featuring 21 feature film World Premieres alongside International and UK Premieres in its Out of Competition strand. Audiences can anticipate the World Premiere of **Chee Keong Cheung**'s thriller **Bad Day at the Office** and the UK Premiere of **Daniel Goldhaber**'s **Faces of Death**. The 2026 festival will open with **Louis Paxton**'s debut feature **The Incomer** and close with **Bel**, further cementing EIFF's role as a vital platform for both established and new cinematic voices.

## A Legacy of Premieres and Independent Spirit

The Edinburgh International Film Festival has long been synonymous with groundbreaking film premieres. Over its storied history, EIFF has been the first major platform for countless films that have gone on to become cultural touchstones. From the gritty realism of **Taxi Driver** and **The Hurt Locker** to the charm of **Amelie** and the iconic sci-fi of **Back to the Future**, Edinburgh has consistently delivered cinematic events that resonate globally. This tradition of unveiling significant works continues under the leadership of CEO and Festival Director **Paul Ridd**, who has been instrumental in shaping the festival's revitalized direction since 2024, alongside Festival Producer **Emma Boa**. Their focus remains on accelerating the discovery of new film talent and fostering deep engagement with audiences, industry professionals, and media on local, national, and international levels.

## For the Passionate Film Fan

For cinephiles and casual moviegoers alike, the announcement of the 2027 dates is a welcome signal of continuity and anticipation. The EIFF isn't just a festival; it's a pilgrimage for those who believe in the power of independent cinema. Knowing that August 2027 will once again bring a curated selection of the world's most exciting new films to Scotland allows fans to plan and dream. The festival's commitment to being the "home of independent cinema in the UK" means that audiences can expect a program that is bold, diverse, and true to the spirit of filmmaking that pushes boundaries and tells essential stories. It’s a chance to connect with the filmmakers shaping the future and to experience cinematic art in one of the world's most beautiful cities.

## What's Next

While the full program for the 80th edition in 2027 is still some time away, the announcement of the dates is the first step in what promises to be another unforgettable celebration of film. Fans can look forward to further details regarding programming, special events, and ticketing information as the festival draws nearer.
